c.tagline: The City of Joy — India's cultural capital of literature, art, adda, and unrivalled street food.

taxi.fareNote: The iconic yellow Ambassador taxis are metered but drivers often refuse the meter or demand a flat fare, especially for short trips; app cabs (Uber/Ola) or the no-refusal yellow-and-blue taxis are usually smoother.

emergency.note: 112 is India's single national emergency number connecting police, fire and ambulance; 108 is the state ambulance service and 100 the direct police line.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in crowds (New Market, Howrah station); touts

hood_desc: Kolkata's cosmopolitan spine — a boulevard of historic restaurants, bars, live-music venues, cafes and hotels, walking distance to the Indian Museum, New Market and the Maidan; the natural base for first-timers who want to be central and lively.

The colonial-era administrative core around Dalhousie Square (BBD Bagh), packed with grand Raj-era architecture like Writers' Building, the GPO and St. John's Church; busy and business-like by day, ideal for heritage walks and history buffs.

A planned, leafy residential and IT township east of the center — Sector V is Kolkata's tech hub — with wide roads, malls like City Centre and the Nicco Park amusement park; calm and modern, suiting families, business travelers and those wanting space.

An affluent, tree-lined South Kolkata neighbourhood of old mansions and upscale apartments anchored by the Gariahat shopping-and-dining belt; refined and local, great for boutique dining, saree markets and a residential feel.

The oldest, most atmospheric part of the city around Shobhabazar and Kumartuli, with narrow lanes, crumbling aristocratic rajbaris, the College Street book market and the idol-makers' workshops; best for heritage, culture and authentic old-Calcutta character.

water.note: Tap water is not safe for visitors; use bottled or filtered water, including for brushing teeth.

transit.hours: Metro runs roughly 6:45 AM to 10:40 PM; buses and trams run through the day with limited late-night service, after which app cabs and yellow taxis fill the gap.
transit.note: Kolkata Metro (opened 1984) is India's oldest metro; the network now runs the north-south Blue Line plus the newer Green Line under the Hooghly River and the Orange and Purple lines. The city also keeps Asia's oldest operating tram network, though it has shrunk to a few heritage routes.
transit.pay: Metro uses tokens, smart cards and QR tickets; buses and trams are paid in cash to the conductor. Fares are very low (metro from ₹5, buses from ₹8).

landmarks: Victoria Memorial
A vast white marble monument set amid manicured gardens, this domed edifice is Kolkata's grandest colonial-era landmark and most photographed building.
Howrah Bridge
The iconic cantilever bridge spanning the Hooghly River, alive with ferries and crowds below, is the defining silhouette of Kolkata's skyline.
Dakshineswar Kali Temple
A riverside temple complex with a towering nine-spired shikhara, famed as the spiritual home of saint Ramakrishna and a serene Hooghly-bank photo spot.
Belur Math
The serene headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission blends Hindu, Islamic, and Christian architectural motifs into one strikingly photogenic temple.
Indian Museum
Asia's oldest and largest museum, housed in a grand colonial building, offers a treasure trove of art, fossils, and antiquities in an elegant courtyard setting.
St. Paul's Cathedral
This Gothic-revival cathedral with a soaring tower and stained glass is one of Kolkata's finest examples of colonial ecclesiastical architecture.
Marble Palace
A 19th-century mansion crammed with sculptures, chandeliers, and marble courtyards, offering a glimpse into aristocratic Bengal splendor.
Kalighat Kali Temple
One of the holiest Shakti Peethas in India, this bustling ancient temple is a vivid, deeply atmospheric pilgrimage and photography site.
Prinsep Ghat
A Palladian-style riverside pavilion on the Hooghly, beautifully lit at sunset, popular for boat rides and skyline photography.
Eden Gardens
India's oldest and most storied cricket stadium, an iconic sporting cathedral synonymous with Kolkata's cricketing passion.

train.note: The Maitree Express to Dhaka and the Bandhan Express to Khulna in Bangladesh have both been suspended since August 2024 and had not resumed by mid-2026, so treat Kolkata as having no working international train. Domestic long-distance services use Howrah and Sealdah stations plus Kolkata (Chitpur) terminal; Howrah is across the river from the centre. Book on IRCTC 60 days ahead - the Rajdhani to Delhi and the Darjeeling Mail to New Jalpaiguri for the hill railway are the ones that sell out.

intl.op: Shyamoli Paribahan — tickets at the Kolkata office, no reliable online booking
Green Line Paribahan — tickets at the Kolkata office

bus.note: Cross-border coaches to Bangladesh leave from the Karunamoyee and Salt Lake terminals rather than the city centre, and take 12 hours or more with a long stop at the Benapole/Petrapole border - carry your passport and a Bangladeshi visa obtained in advance. Domestic buses are run by WBTC (https://wbtconline.in/) and private operators bookable through redBus (https://www.redbus.in/). Esplanade is the main city departure point for Digha and other Bengal destinations.

ferry.note: There is no international ferry from Kolkata. Local launches cross the Hooghly between Howrah, Babughat and Bagbazar as a fast commuter alternative to the bridges, run by the West Bengal Transport Corporation, and cruise boats run downriver to the Sundarbans as tours rather than scheduled transport.

half.name: Diamond Harbour
half.blurb: A Hooghly River port about 50 kilometers south of Kolkata with a ruined colonial fort, jetty views, and boat rides toward the river mouth.

half.name: Serampore
half.blurb: A former Danish trading colony on the Hooghly River north of Kolkata, home to Serampore College and riverside colonial buildings from the early 1800s.

full.name: Shantiniketan
full.blurb: Rabindranath Tagore's university town about 160 kilometers northwest of Kolkata, with the Visva-Bharati campus, his ashram, and a UNESCO-listed cultural district.

full.name: Bishnupur
full.blurb: A former Malla-dynasty capital roughly 150 kilometers from Kolkata known for terracotta Hindu temples decorated with carved brick panels from the 17th century.

full.name: Sundarbans National Park
full.blurb: A mangrove delta and tiger reserve southeast of Kolkata reached by road and boat, with wildlife-spotting cruises through tidal channels shared with Bangladesh.
